question:
A 18-year-old man experiencing homelessness is brought to the emergency department by law
enforcement after being found minimally responsive at a mall. His medical history includes
polysubstance abuse, anxiety, depression, and panic disorder. His current medications are sertraline,
clonazepam, and amitriptyline. Vital signs show: - Temperature: 98.7°F (37.1°C) - Blood pressure:
117/68 mmHg - Pulse: 80/min - Respirations: 10/min - Oxygen saturation: 98% on room air On
examination, he is somnolent with 4 mm pupils that are equal and reactive. When stimulated, he
responds incoherently. His bowel sounds are normal, and his abdomen is non-tender. Laboratory
results show: - Na+: 139 mEq/L - Cl-: 100 mEq/L - K+: 4.3 mEq/L - HCO3-: 25 mEq/L - BUN: 20 mg/dL
- Glucose: 99 mg/dL - Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL - Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL - Ethanol: negative ECG is
unremarkable. What is the most appropriate treatment for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Bretazenil
(B) Supportive care with IV fluids (C) Hemodialysis (D) Gastric lavage (E) Physostigmine (F) Naloxone
(G) Activated charcoal (H) Flumazenil (I) IV sodium bicarbonate (J) Observation
 A. Bretazenil
B. Naloxone
C. Supportive care with IV fluids
D. Observation
E. Activated charcoal
F. Gastric lavage
G. IV sodium bicarbonate
H. Flumazenil
I. Hemodialysis
J. Physostigmine
